exposure: Type of emergency obstetric care intervention (medical, surgical)
cohort: The study included 153 queens of various breeds and ages that presented to the clinic with dystocia.
finding: Medical management for feline dystocia was successful in only a minority of cases (17%), while singleton pregnancy and prolonged duration of labor were associated with an increased risk of difficult labor and stillbirth.
mod_finding: Pregnancy after caesarean section is possible, with some queens achieving successful natural births.
